title: fix: publish UI package through npm OIDC
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Grants the UI release job GitHub OIDC permission and removes its `NPM_TOKEN` dependency.
- Triggers the UI job when this workflow changes, so the unpublished `0.1.0-alpha.3` is retried after merge.
- Before merge, an npm package owner must add a Trusted Publisher for `@pollinations/ui`: GitHub repository `pollinations/pollinations`, workflow `release-publish-npm-packages.yml`, with `npm publish` allowed. This npm setting cannot be changed in a GitHub PR.
- After merge, verify the release run and `npm view @pollinations/ui dist-tags` reports `alpha: 0.1.0-alpha.3`.

Addresses the [failed release](https://github.com/pollinations/pollinations/actions/runs/35786203865).

gist.headline: The UI gets a passport
gist.blurb: The UI package release job now uses GitHub’s OIDC passport instead of keeping an npm token in its pocket. Once npm trusts the publisher, alpha.3 can finally leave the nest.
gist.summary: The npm release workflow now grants the @pollinations/ui publish job GitHub OIDC permissions, removes its NPM_TOKEN dependency, and reruns when the workflow changes so @pollinations/ui@0.1.0-alpha.3 can publish under npm Trusted Publishing.
gist.impact: Developers can receive the @pollinations/ui alpha dist-tag through a tokenless, GitHub-attested publishing path once the npm Trusted Publisher is configured.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy package-post office represents the UI package finally being sent out: Polli wears a tiny postal cap and presents a glowing OIDC passport beside a small @pollinations/ui parcel, while a friendly CRT robot checks the trusted-publisher stamp. A code-flower garden and lime-green release conveyor make the security-and-release workflow feel welcoming rather than bureaucratic.
